note: Money and Macro discusses the paradox that we see low risk big blockbusters that make a profusion sequals and content primarily from established franchises while still having a rich long tail of independent contant. The idea is that big budget studios only invest in superstars (> $150M+) which favors established franchises while smaller projects get the lower tiered funding (< $10M-). Interesting, there seems to be a dead zone around $10M-$150M (for movies at least).
